commands_used: answer 1. I work for Nesh-Deeka of the Toh-Reel-Ka in Helstrom. I recovered a Kothringi Keystone from the Pale Harvest wreck. The Collector (Ennodius Vanin) and the Unbound are hunting the Eye, and the keystone seems tied to it. 2. Go to Toklea, find Hums-the-Long-Note (quest marker), and show the keystone to the Chime-Keepers elder in the Kothringi Greathouse. 3. I can talk to Hums-the-Long-Note, ask about the elder, or show the keystone. I should stay quiet and careful, since others hunt this. 4. I do not know who Hums-the-Long-Note is, what the Eye is, or what the keystone does. I could find out by asking the Chime-Keepers.

answer 1. Hums-the-Long-Note is the Chime-Keepers elder. She knows the keystone but wants payment first: her family grave-stake from a chest in drowned Zul-Etha. 2. Go to Zul-Etha (from Mir-Xal quay, south-east), reach the Drowned Chest, raise the grave-stake, bring it back to her. 3. Kill the crocodiles and old bull from a roof or with arrows, calm them with Illusion, or swim under them unseen. Quiet fits my build, so swimming or sneaking is best. 4. I do not know where exactly Mir-Xal quay is relative to here, or whether the chest is locked. I can find out via the map marker and by looking.

answer 1. I have the grave-stake from the chest without disturbing the crocodiles. Hums-the-Long-Note will tell me about the keystone in return. 2. Bring the stake to Hums-the-Long-Note in Toklea. 3. Just return and hand it over; then ask about the keystone. 4. I still do not know what the keystone does or what the Eye is; Hums should tell me.

answer 1. Hums kept her word: the keystone opens the tomb of the knight-captain at Eurydike, a ruin north of Gideon. The knights guarded the kings road to the Root. 2. Tell Nesh-Deeka in Helstrom. 3. Go straight to Nesh-Deeka, or perhaps visit Eurydike myself later; the journal asks me to report first. 4. I do not know what the Root is exactly, nor what the captain was buried with. Nesh-Deeka or the tomb may tell me.

answer 1. The quest is done. I learned the keystone opens the knight-captain tomb at Eurydike near Gideon, which holds what marked the way to the Root. The Unbound are already asking about Eurydike, and Nesh-Deeka wants me quick. She paid me 100 gold. 2. Nothing is set; the likely next step is to go to Eurydike near Gideon before the Unbound. 3. Go to Eurydike myself and open the tomb quietly, or ask Nesh-Deeka more. 4. I do not know what the Root is, what the Eye is, or how Nesh-Deeka listens.

answer I am a Voh-Vastei of the Toh-Reel-Ka under Nesh-Deeka in Helstrom. Hums-the-Long-Note, elder of the Chime-Keepers in Toklea, told me the Kothringi Keystone opens the knight-captain tomb at Eurydike, a roofless Kothringi hall a short walk north of Gideon. The knights of Gideon guarded the old kings road to the Root, and the captain was buried with what marked the way. I paid her price by taking her family grave-stake from the chest in drowned Zul-Etha, without fighting the crocodiles. I reported to Nesh-Deeka, who paid 100 gold (about 700 total). She says the Unbound are already asking Gideon diggers about Eurydike, so we must be quick. She only said "we listen" about how she knows. I still carry the Keystone, Pale Harvest Strongbox Key, Old Silver Setting, The Collector note and the smuggler key. Open questions: what the Eye and the Root are, and what the tomb holds. The Collector (Ennodius Vanin) and the Unbound are still hunting. Next: go to Eurydike quietly and open the tomb.
